minutes.headline: Board recommended most Town Meeting articles, deferred some, and with assessors set Jan 6 as tax bill mailing date.
minutes.summary: After a closed session on the fire union contract, the board heard public comment on abatements and a school bus policy update, made appointments, and voted recommendations on the town meeting warrant. A joint workshop with the Board of Assessors covered abatement timing, hearing access, and the investigation's core questions. The assessors voted to set the bill mailing date as January 6th.

public_comment.topic: Asked when the same effort used on the mailing date will be applied to the 135 percent waterfront land increase and the sales used.
Asked how the abatement process works and whether applicants can attend deliberations.
Asked about work handover between interim and later principal assessor.
Questioned oversight of the principal assessor and the town's organizational structure.
Cautioned that a 90-day extension pushes into FY24 and urged faster hearings.
Asked about access to the re-inspection report, ATB timelines, and how decisions will be communicated.
Asked for a date for the principal assessor's presentation and raised DOR sales standard.
Questioned how abatements could be denied given a 135 percent land increase.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 4-0 to recommend most Town Meeting warrant articles, including the omnibus budget, capital plan, stabilization, OPEB and senior tax relief.
The board deferred the firefighters union contract article and the sewer enterprise budget, the latter because the Sewer Commission has not voted its final number.
In a joint workshop, the Board of Assessors voted 3-0 to set January 6 as the mailing date for the third and fourth quarter tax bills.
The board asked the assessors for a written abatement review process within about a week, with a published schedule.
Residents pressed on abatement hearings, a land value increase and the timing of decisions, and the board also made three appointments.

why_it_matters: The January 6 mailing date sets when the later tax bills are due and when interest begins, and the unsettled abatement process decides how and when residents can contest their assessments.
The recommendations and deferrals shape what voters will be asked to approve at Town Meeting, including the budget, reserve transfers and the pending firefighters contract and sewer budget.
watch_next: The assessors' written abatement review process and published schedule, due within about a week.
The deferred articles on the firefighters union contract and the sewer enterprise budget, and the Town Meeting votes on the warrant.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on most Select Board votes and on the figures for Articles 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 15, 16, 17 and 18. They differ on four votes our recording has and the official text does not (Salary Administration Plan, Articles 3, 12 and 14), and on how Article 4 and the attendee names are given. A reader should check those four votes, because the official minutes record no vote on them and we recorded a recommendation or deferral on each.
